cells.tense: The scales sit level and your hand is on the beam right now.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: When a split comes up with someone close, settle it from the middle, then set down whatever you have been carrying on their behalf. Bring the account in plain words, nothing else — that step toward them is the whole move.
cells.core:
You can sit at an uneven table and wait. While the argument runs, you hold off while the weight of each side shows, then you set the beam level. Nobody is crushed and nothing important gets dropped. That is what your stillness is for, and it is why people bring you the things they cannot split themselves.

It runs on a light touch. How fair your call comes out depends on how little you carried in with you, and some of what you are holding belongs to their side, not yours. Before the next split, move toward what still connects you and put a borrowed piece down. One copy of the account, in plain words, both names on it, is enough. Then you can settle it, and you are both still sitting there.
cells.sheetLine: You even the split by knowing what isn't yours to carry.
cells.place: at the table where the split gets made fair

cells.tense: The scales will be braced against a verdict nobody has brought yet.
cells.act: refuse the pull off course, once more
cells.ask: The next time someone leans on you to redraw a split their way, say the number you worked out and stop — one sentence, no going back over it later. The total you reached is the one that holds.
cells.core:
You are bracing the beam for an argument that hasn't arrived. Every division gets reworked in your head before the other person has opened their mouth, and more keeps coming off your own side to keep things even. What was careful weighing turns into a position staked against somebody who is not there yet. The people close to you get handed a ruling, not a scale.

This has a cost, and the paying of it is familiar. The next time the pull starts, say your number once and stand behind it — no checking it after. That will feel like leaving a door ajar, and you can leave it that way. In the morning the line you drew is still where you put it and nothing has tipped. If the sum was wrong, that will show by itself, and you can look again then.
cells.sheetLine: You get the scales set before anyone has spoken.
cells.place: at the table where the split gets made fair

cells.tense: The fair split was made some while back and you have not returned to it.
cells.act: go once toward the thing that draws you and see what it is up close
cells.ask: Something keeps tugging at you and you keep not going. Go once this week and look at it plainly for an afternoon — alone, nothing decided, nobody told.
cells.core:
The weighing was finished and you have not been back near it. At the table where things get levelled, the chair is empty. From outside you look steady. Inside, nothing is being brought in to be measured at all — no want, no complaint, no case of your own.

Trying to make yourself care will not help, and it is not needed. Follow a pull a little way instead — the one that keeps drawing you and gets nowhere in particular — and just go look at it once, up close. Move toward it with nothing settled on your side. What you find there may be small or may be nothing. Either way the scale starts moving again, and it moves at your size, not someone else's.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the scales even and leave yourself off them.
cells.place: at the table where the split gets made fair

cells.tense: The level split is being held for all of them and your account is that you only listened.
cells.act: leave the hollow ritual for the living one
cells.ask: Take one standing arrangement in your week that has gone mechanical and do it differently once — for a reason you picked this week, not to keep the circle whole. One time through is enough.
cells.core:
You are the one evening the split when nobody has asked you to. In the last stretch a call was held off, a word was chosen carefully, a sum quietly came out of your side and evened the whole thing — and your account of it is that you were only being fair, or only listening. The beam sits level because somebody reached in and set it. Nobody watching has grounds to say otherwise.

Turn one of those standing arrangements back into something alive. Swap out a routine kept going out of habit and do it once for a reason you actually chose this week. The old shape may feel thinner than the honest one. That thinness is only where your hand was not showing. Now it does.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness comes from you, and you'd call it listening.
cells.place: at the table where the split gets made fair

attempts.check: The record says the mind rests before it strategizes; it never says the person handles anything well, so a core that claims a settled skill in the chair would be overreach. A reader could fairly say the slower settlement is just tiredness or an off day, not a bent capacity — which is why the ask leans on the person's own copy rather than on anyone else noticing, and stays useful if the read is wrong. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is the one about the mind lying still on purpose — it sounds settled, so each core spends it somewhere the person could recognise instead.
